<Subject 1>【一秋】 is the young woman in <Picture 1>; her face, hair and identity strictly follow <Picture 1>. Her black hair is parted in the middle and gathered into a low bun fixed with two light-wood hairpins; she wears a fine gold necklace with a small pendant, a plain unbleached-linen crossed-collar long robe with wide sleeves over a white inner dress, a pale-beige fabric sash tied at the waist with two long hanging ends, a very long flowing layered white skirt, and white flat cloth shoes. She starts with both hands gently clasped in front of her waist and holds no props. Her dance motion comes from <Video 1>. (character definition, never spoken aloud)
<Subject 2> is the rural Tujia mountain-village square in <Picture 1>: a ground paved with irregular grey stone slabs, dark timber stilt houses with black tiled roofs and white upturned gable ridges, red lanterns hanging under the eaves, a green leafy tree on the left, a black iron lamp post with square blue-and-white lanterns on the right, and a forested mountain slope under a pale overcast sky behind; in the far background, villagers and visitors are seated at long tables on small stools for an open-air village gathering.
<Subject 3> is the decoration on the fully opened skirt disc, visible only in the final part: an ivory-white linen circular ground with a thin tea-green and gold scalloped rim; two symmetrical vine-tea vines climb up the left and right, rendered in tea-green with gold outlines, with curling tendrils, tender buds and tiny white frost flecks on the leaves; at the center sits an earthen Tujia clay teapot with a small tea bowl filled with pale-green vine tea, faint steam rising; at the top center are four large golden Chinese calligraphy characters 来凤藤茶.
<Video 1> is the reference dance video: it provides the full seven-second temporal structure, the stepping into a self-spin and folding into a deep back-bend, the skirt's flaring physics and timing, and the tripod-locked front-facing vertical framing.
<Video 2> is the grayscale depth-motion video extracted from <Video 1>: it guides only the figure's silhouette, the spine-bending path, and the circular expansion geometry of the skirt disc, and carries no color, face, costume or texture.
<Picture 1> is the character and scene reference image, showing the woman in a plain white linen robe standing on a stone-paved village square with timber houses and a forested hillside behind.

detailed_description:
The target video is a cinematic, realistic live-action rural ethnic-dance showcase in a vertical 9:16 frame, set on a stone-paved village square in soft overcast daylight; the light is even and diffused with gentle shadows, the timber houses and forested hillside show muted natural tones, and the grey stone slabs carry a faint damp sheen.
A single continuous tripod-locked full-body medium-long shot from start to finish, front-facing with the dancer centered, exactly as in <Video 1>; the framing never changes, with no cut, no second camera and no handheld movement.
Acting direction for the whole sequence: she is a real dancer performing a rehearsed showcase move rather than posing for the camera; the spin carries all her momentum and she commits her full body weight into the bend. Nobody speaks, sings or narrates at any point; the sequence is carried only by movement, fabric and village ambience.
The shot opens on <Subject 1> standing still and centered, facing the camera, hands gently clasped in front of her waist, the long white layered skirt resting on the stone slabs around her feet; the two wood hairpins and the gold pendant catch the soft daylight.
She steps out and sweeps both wide sleeves open, launching into a fast on-the-spot self-spin; the linen robe and the long white skirt lift and spiral around her, the two beige sash ends fly outward, and the gold pendant and hairpins sway with the turn.
Keeping the spin, she folds her body downward into a deep back-bend, tilting her head toward the ground and planting one palm flat on the stone slabs to support her weight while her other arm reaches out to the side; driven by the spin's momentum, the long layered white skirt whips upward and outward over her bent body and opens into a giant near-perfect horizontal disc, its decorated inner surface facing the camera like a huge round paper fan.
The ivory-white disc fills most of the frame width and gently rotates into place as the motion settles: it is <Subject 3>, with two symmetrical vine-tea vines climbing the left and right in rich tea-green with gold outlines, curling tendrils, tender buds and tiny white frost flecks; at the center sits an earthen Tujia clay teapot beside a small tea bowl filled with pale-green vine tea with faint steam rising; and at the top-center of the disc are the four large golden Chinese calligraphy characters 来凤藤茶, rendered clearly and correctly, framed by a thin tea-green and gold scalloped rim.
Below the disc, <Subject 1> holds the back-bend, one palm flat on the stone slabs, head tilted down, the wide sleeves and beige sash hanging and trembling softly; the huge white skirt disc holds its open shape above her with only soft fabric ripples until the final frame.
The camera stays perfectly still throughout; the timber houses, red lanterns, the leafy tree and the distant long-table gathering remain softly out of focus behind her, the villagers visible only as gentle background silhouettes, while the diffused daylight stays steady.
The frame contains no subtitles, no watermarks and no logos; the only legible Chinese characters are the four golden characters 来凤藤茶 on the opened skirt, rendered exactly as given, and all background signs and lanterns remain softly out of focus with no readable text.

overall_soundscape:
A quiet mountain-village square in overcast daylight, with a soft breeze, distant birdsong from the hillside, and faint cheerful chatter and clatter of the open-air long-table gathering far behind. The long layered linen skirt gives a heavy airy whump and rustle as it spins and flares open, settling into stillness as the disc opens.
